help.title: Help and shortcuts
help.whatBody: An editor for radiometric FLIR thermal photos. Remap the palette, correct the calibration parameters, measure areas and temperatures and export ready-to-use images — one at a time, in bulk or by folder. All processing happens in the browser: no file is uploaded online. The only exception is the map view, which downloads the cartography tiles from an external provider.
help.exportBody1: An image's ZIP contains the clean thermal, the annotated thermal, the visible photo and — if you enabled it — the overlay, plus aree.csv and the .json session. “Include originals” adds the source FLIR photos (the ZIP gets much larger, but the work reopens anywhere).
help.exportBody2: “Save session” exports only the .json: a lightweight checkpoint you reopen by dragging it onto the image, or onto the folder. To align palette, parameters or areas across several photos use “Apply settings” in the filmstrip.

map.playTourTitle: Fly over every photo in capture order
map.tourPanel: Tour of the photos on the map
map.noGpsBody: The open photos contain no GPS tag in their EXIF, so there is nothing to place.
map.noGpsLink: Open them in Geotag to place them by hand →
map.consentBody: To draw the map, the browser must download cartography tiles from an external provider (OpenFreeMap, Esri or OpenStreetMap). It is the only feature of Warmish that connects to the internet: the provider receives your IP address and the area you are viewing. No image, coordinate or thermal data leaves your device.
map.consentDeniedBody: You chose not to load the base cartography. The map stays disabled; everything else in Warmish works normally.
map.popupSameCoord: Every GPS photo has this same coordinate — the camera recorded a single position for the session, not one per shot.
map.popupSameCoordLink: Place them by hand in Geotag →
map.minimalUnavailable: "Minimal" basemap unavailable, falling back to Esri.
